featured_videos.commentary: The comments section here is honestly telling. people are tired of the performative debates, but they're also hungry for the actual nuance. Dr. Lily's getting heat for exploring complexity instead of just picking a team, which says a lot about where we are right now. featured_videos.title: My First Week on Carnivore: What I Wish I Knew
featured_videos.creator: The Daily Ribeye
featured_videos.editorial_title: My First Week on Carnivore: What I Wish I Knew
featured_videos.commentary: The thing that jumps out here is how honest you two are about the messy first week. literally. That comment about "striping the bowl" got real laughs, but it's exactly why so many people quit before they see results. Your body's adjusting to processing fat way differently than it did on carbs, and yeah, some folks need to dial back the fat intake while their bile production catches up. What's beautiful is watching the community validate what you're experiencing. You've got someone 14 months in feeling fantastic, another person down 13 pounds in three weeks with mental clarity they didn't expect, and a 65-year-old reversing pre-diabetes and ditching blood pressure meds. That's not hype. that's what actually happens when people stick past week one. The wins you're already seeing in energy and clarity? That's just the beginning.

featured_videos.title: Why Your Glucose Is Going UP on Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Jenny Mitich
featured_videos.editorial_title: Why Your Glucose Is Going UP on Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: One comment really stuck with me: someone tracked their fasting glucose jumping from the high 80s on keto to mid-100s on carnivore, but their HbA1C stayed solid at 5.6/5.7. That's the whole story right there, and it's why Jenny's video matters so much. People see a single fasting glucose number and panic, but they're missing the context that gluconeogenesis is doing exactly what it's supposed to do, converting your body fat into fuel. The timing of your last meal, how much protein you actually ate, and whether you're measuring during your dawn phenomenon spike all change what that number means. If you're worried about this, a CGM will show you your actual glucose trends instead of letting a single test result scare you into thinking carnivore broke your metabolism. It didn't.

featured_videos.title: Will the CARNIVORE DIET Finally Help Me Lose 100 Pounds?!?
featured_videos.creator: My Lilac Hill Homestead (My Lilac Hill)
featured_videos.editorial_title: Will the CARNIVORE DIET Finally Help Me Lose 100 Pounds?!?
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here tell the real story. A 65-year-old moving from a wheelchair to a cane. Someone going from 300+ pounds and homelessness to off all medications and hiking mountains. These aren't before-and-after photos with a sales pitch attached, they're people saying "this actually works." The big takeaway I'm seeing isn't just weight loss, it's the stuff nobody talks about until it's gone: the pain disappearing, the energy coming back, the mental clarity. One commenter nailed it when they mentioned that even on keto, you can still overeat meat if you're not paying attention. That's the honest part carnivore community doesn't shy away from. The diet removes a lot of barriers (no shopping complexity, no constant hunger), but it still requires you to actually commit. If you're watching this video right now thinking about jumping in, the pattern in these comments is consistent: start strict, dial in your protocol, and give it time. The results show up faster than people expect.

featured_videos.title: What I Buy at Costco for a Carnivore Diet
featured_videos.creator: Tatiana Timofeyev
featured_videos.editorial_title: What I Buy at Costco for a Carnivore Diet
featured_videos.commentary: What I love about Tatiana's approach is how unglamorous it is, which honestly makes it the most useful. No fancy recipes, no supplement stacks, no "biohacking". just showing up at Costco and grabbing what actually works. That comment about keeping things simple instead of chasing complicated recipes hit the mark, because the people who stick with carnivore long-term are the ones who make it boring enough to maintain. And yeah, having those protein options ready to go (the fish, the ground beef, the eggs) is what separates a sustainable eating plan from another diet you'll quit in three months. The practical wins matter way more than the Instagram-worthy ones.
